$comment: TWO expectations per case, not one binary label.
`grammarValid` is what the runtime reader applies on every dev server and
every build, and what the scaffolder must agree with. `submissionProfileValid`
is the bounded operational profile — length, no build metadata, numeric
identifiers a comparator can order — and applies only where a manifest is
built, a ZIP is named, or a URL path is generated.
Conflating them would put a 128-character cap into the reader that runs on
every `vite dev`, which is a submission concern failing an ordinary build.

cases.why: SemVer excludes build metadata from precedence, so 1.0.0+a and 1.0.0+b tie for a latest endpoint
the largest core component node-semver accepts
node-semver@7.8.5 rejects this outright, so a grammar-only reader would admit a version the agreed comparator refuses
this and 1.0.0-100000000000000000000 are distinct strings that compare EQUAL, so two identities would tie with no defined order
the other half of the tie
129 characters — it becomes a ZIP filename and a URL path segment
never trimmed: whitespace makes an identity string invalid, not trimmable
leading zeroes in a core component
leading zeroes in a numeric prerelease identifier
